source_name: World Health Organization (WHO) Basic Emergency Care
description: Standardized life-saving interventions for acute trauma and critical illness.
text: The WHO Basic Emergency Care (BEC) framework follows the ABCDE resuscitation priority: A - Airway: Ensure patent airway without obstruction. Use chin lift/jaw thrust. B - Breathing: Assess chest rise, respiratory rate, and oxygenation. C - Circulation: Control catastrophic external hemorrhage with direct pressure or tourniquet. Assess pulse and capillary refill. D - Disability: Check neurological responsiveness via AVPU scale (Alert, Voice, Pain, Unresponsive). E - Exposure: Prevent hypothermia by keeping trauma patients warm.

source_name: Indian Red Cross Society First Aid Manual
description: Community first aid guidelines for CPR, burns, fractures, and heatstroke.
text: Adult CPR: If an adult is unresponsive and not breathing, initiate chest compressions immediately in the center of the chest. Push hard and fast at 100-120 compressions per minute to a depth of 5-6 cm. For thermal burns, cool the affected area under gentle running water for at least 10-20 minutes. Never apply ice, butter, oil, or toothpaste to burns. For heatstroke (body temperature > 40°C), move the person to a cool area, loosen clothing, apply cold wet cloths to armpits, groin, and neck, and call emergency services.

description: National Disaster Management Authority CAP-based early warning dissemination system.
text: SACHET is the Indian National Early Warning dissemination platform for cyclones, floods, tsunamis, landslides, and earthquakes. During an earthquake: Drop to the floor, take Cover under a sturdy table, and Hold on until shaking ceases. During cyclone alerts: Board up loose glass windows, store 72 hours of non-perishable food and potable water, keep battery radios ready, and disconnect electrical appliances before evacuation.

description: National meteorological observations, severe weather color-coded warnings (Green, Yellow, Orange, Red).
text: IMD issues four-color weather alerts: Green (No warning / normal), Yellow (Be updated / watch), Orange (Be prepared / alert), and Red (Take action / emergency response). For thunderstorms and lightning, follow the 30/30 rule: if the time between lightning flash and thunder is less than 30 seconds, seek substantial enclosed shelter immediately. Stay inside for at least 30 minutes after the last thunderclap.
